title: Java Output
learningObjectives: Use System.out.println to display text followed by a line break.
Use System.out.print to display text without automatically ending the line.
Display the values of variables and expressions.
Use printf with common format specifiers for formatted output.
Predict the visible output of short Java output statements.

understand.concept: Java provides standard output through `System.out`. The `print` method writes output without automatically adding a line break, while `println` writes output and then ends the line. The `printf` method formats values using specifiers such as `%s` for text, `%d` for integral values and `%.2f` for a floating-point value with two digits after the decimal point.
understand.whyItMatters: Programs communicate results through output. Clear output helps users understand what a program did and helps developers inspect values while testing.
understand.analogy: print writes on the same line; println writes and moves to the next line; printf fills a formatted output pattern.
understand.analogyLimit: Formatted output does not validate business data or guarantee a locale-independent display. Floating-point rounding, locale settings and format mismatches can affect results.

explain.narrative:
## print and println

`System.out.print("Hello")` writes text and leaves the cursor on the same line. `System.out.println("World")` writes text and then moves to a new line.

## Display values

You can pass a variable or expression to print and println. Java evaluates the expression and converts supported values to text for display.

## Formatted output with printf

`System.out.printf` accepts a format string and values. `%s` formats text, `%d` formats integral values and `%.2f` formats a floating-point value with two digits after the decimal point. `%n` requests a platform-appropriate line separator.

Choose a format specifier that matches the value type. For financial applications, do not assume binary floating-point alone is an appropriate money representation.

practise.guidedTask: Write three output statements: one using print, one using println and one using printf. Predict where each line break appears before running the program.
practise.independentTask: Display a product name, quantity and unit price using printf. Use an integer format for quantity and a two-decimal floating-point format for the sample price. Explain why display formatting alone does not make floating-point arithmetic suitable for every financial calculation.
